changes.headline: Monday settled a dollar lower, Asia took another, and December WCS widened again on thin volume while the traded export spread narrowed
changes.dek: Monday settles: Brent $115.81 (was $116.72 Friday), WTI $101.76 (was $103.27); the deep late prints near $114.20 were intraday, not settles. Asia at 0418 GMT Tue: Brent $114.81, WTI $100.88 (Reuters). ICE Oct 26: TMW Dec26 -$29.25 on 50 lots (was -$28.50 on 555 lots Friday); ARV to TMW January +$7.80 traded both sides (was +$8.35). Diesel crack $98.16, a third print below $100.. Brent touched $117 intraday on Monday, dipped toward $114.50 in the European morning, and settled at $115.81, down $0.91; WTI settled at $101.76, down $1.51, with the Brent to WTI spread widening to $14.05 at the settle. Overnight, Asia traded Brent at $114.81 and WTI at $100.88 at 0418 GMT (Reuters, Oct 27), a second down day carried on diplomacy headlines: officials from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey met Iranian leaders in Tehran on Monday and agreed to continue talks, with no agreement, no measures and no date set. Monday's ICE file widened December WCS a second day, to -$29.25 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 26), but on only 50 lots against Friday's 555, while January widened to -$28.20 on 275 lots. December's export spread print (+$7.25) rests on an untraded ARV leg; the January spread narrowed to +$7.80 from +$8.35 with both legs traded. December WCS outright is $72.51. Synthetic settled +$5.75 on zero lots, an untraded mark; Friday's traded +$5.70 on 300 lots remains the verdict print. The diesel crack printed $98.16 on the validated history refreshed this edition, below $100 for a third print (3-2-1: $52.85).
changes.balance_read: The pullback is grading claims, not barrels: no confirmed Saudi damage, Yanbu flowing on tracker data, and Tehran only talking, against flow gauges that still point tight (ANZ: Gulf exports down four straight weeks, Hormuz at about 60 percent of normal). In Canada the front keeps widening into November apportionment but on thinning volume, while the traded export spread narrows from the ICE legs after the freight correction.

changes.headline: A tanker was disabled in Hormuz on Oct 23, disclosed Monday; the Saudi damage ledger stays empty and the minister's venue was Singapore
changes.dek: New versus Monday's edition: UKMTO verified an outbound tanker struck by an unknown projectile on Oct 23 and disabled, crew safe, reported three days late. Monday's Houthi claim named the East-West pumping stations; no Saudi confirmation. Argus: Shaybah and Yanbu undamaged. Kpler: Yanbu loaded 2.21 Mb/d Oct 1 to 25. Correction: no Bahrain keynote was reported; the Saudi energy minister keynoted in Singapore and Aramco agreed Jurong storage from H2 2027.. UKMTO disclosed on Monday a verified report that a tanker transiting outbound through the Strait of Hormuz was struck by an unknown projectile at 08:39 UTC on Oct 23 and disabled, all crew safe, with no damage extent published (UKMTO, Oct 26). It is the first verified disablement of this claim cycle, and it arrived three days late because owners are largely not reporting incidents. A second UKMTO item, third party reports of a vessel on fire southeast of Al-Faw, is classified suspicious activity, not a confirmed attack. JMIC's Oct 25 advisory holds the Strait at SEVERE with about 492 vessels waiting outside it; CENTCOM (Oct 25) says the primary lanes are free of Iranian mines and counts more than 1.5 billion barrels exported with US support since summer, cumulative assisted figures rather than a flow rate. On the Saudi side, Monday's Houthi claim on the East-West pumping stations and Riyadh airport drew no Saudi confirmation; the coalition destroyed two launchers in Sanaa. An Argus source said Shaybah and Yanbu were undamaged, and Kpler puts Saudi exports at 5.52 Mb/d for Oct 1 to 25 with Yanbu at 2.21 Mb/d, down from 2.54 in September: the bypass flowed through the claim window at a lower rate. The Saudi energy minister's documented venue on Monday was the Singapore International Energy Week, where he cited the East-West Pipeline's resilience and Aramco agreed to store crude at Jurong Rock Caverns from the second half of 2027 (about 9 Mbbl).
changes.balance_read: The claim ledger and the hull ledger have diverged: claimed infrastructure damage keeps failing to confirm while verified ship damage accumulates one hull at a time. Confirmed crude flow loss remains zero; the cost is being paid in shipping, waiting fleets and a strategic reserve at a 44 year low (SPR 282.6 Mbbl, week ending Oct 23), not in stopped exports.

changes.headline: The TD3C benchmark is on trial in London; Ukraine's refinery claims stay unconfirmed; DOE is silent and the SPR is at a 44 year low
changes.dek: The Mercuria v Baltic trial opened Monday: the opening filing aired panellists calling March to April TD3C assessments a lottery; the Baltic countered in kind. No judgment. Ukraine's Oct 25 to 26 claims on Tuapse, Ryazan and Syzran drew no confirmation Monday. DOE: no new petroleum item, no award for either exchange round, posted contracts at 133.56 Mbbl; SPR 282.6 Mbbl (week ending Oct 23), lowest since October 1982. NEHHOR bids close today at 11:00 a.m. CT.. The trial over whether the Baltic Exchange should have suspended the TD3C benchmark during the Hormuz closure opened Monday in London (Lloyd's List, Oct 26, paywalled, summarized). Mercuria's opening filing quotes TD3C panellists calling the March to April assessments purely hypothetical, complete nonsense, a lottery and academic while the strait was closed, and an internal assessor declining to enter his own control number for almost three weeks. The Baltic says panellists confirmed they could assess and alleges the claim is driven by index linked exposures Mercuria failed to risk manage. TD3C continues to publish (Week 43: WS 1208.13) and no print stands invalidated. On Russia, no confirmation arrived Monday for the claimed strikes on Tuapse, Ryazan and Syzran; the last confirmed refinery strike remains Ryazan on Oct 15, and Russian refiners are reported raising diesel output in October under new export quotas, with no new waiver cargo named. DOE pages checked directly are unchanged since Oct 23, both exchange award rounds remain unpublished six days past the re-offer deadline, and the Northeast heating oil reserve bid deadline is today.
changes.balance_read: Three slow variables moved while flat price took the headlines: the freight benchmark's credibility is now a court record, the Russian refinery campaign's confirmation rate is falling even as its claim rate holds, and the US reserve buffer keeps shrinking without any new award machinery catching up.

flags.title: Hormuz: a verified tanker disablement (Oct 23, disclosed Oct 26); JMIC at SEVERE; the Saudi claims ledger still has no confirmed damage
flags.detail: UKMTO verified that an outbound tanker was struck by an unknown projectile on Oct 23 in the Strait of Hormuz and disabled, crew safe; the report arrived three days late because owners are largely not reporting. JMIC (Oct 25) holds the Strait at SEVERE, counts 156 confirmed regional incidents since Mar 1 and about 492 vessels waiting outside the Strait. CENTCOM (Oct 25) says the primary lanes are mine free and counts more than 1.5 billion barrels exported with US support since summer, cumulative assisted figures, not a flow rate; ANZ (Oct 27) puts Hormuz flows at about 60 percent of normal with Gulf exports down a fourth straight week. Against that, the claimed Saudi damage remains unconfirmed: an Argus source says Shaybah and Yanbu were undamaged, Kpler has Yanbu loading 2.21 Mb/d across Oct 1 to 25, and Monday's claim on the East-West pumping stations drew no Saudi confirmation. The Revolutionary Guards' Oct 24 mine claim still names no ship. Trade the verified hulls and the flow prints, not the claim count. Trigger: A named vessel or corroboration for the mine claim, a Saudi statement of facility damage or a pipeline flow interruption, or a tier 1 flow print stepping down

flags.title: Sanctions waiver: first US cargo at sea; November tranche is the supply test; refiners raising diesel output under new quotas
flags.detail: The first tanker under the waiver loaded 40,000 tonnes of diesel at Primorsk on Oct 22 and is heading for New York, arrival estimated Nov 7 (Reuters, shipping data). No signed supply contracts have been confirmed and no further loading has been reported. Reuters sources (Oct 26) say Russian refiners are raising diesel production in October after the government granted export quotas following the US agreement; no cargo was named. Slovakia's prime minister said after meeting Putin on Oct 23 that there is no official deal on Russian diesel exports to the United States and no exports yet (Reuters). The announced programme runs 500,000 tonnes in November and 1 million tonnes thereafter. The binding constraint is Russian refining capacity: the Ryazan primary unit is halted since Oct 15 and the plant was claimed struck again overnight Oct 25 to 26 without confirmation. The import licence runs to Apr 7, 2027 and the waiver has no fixed expiry. Trigger: A first loading for the November tranche, a named US buyer or signed contract confirmation, a Ryazan restart report, or a move in Congress to block the arrangement

flags.title: November apportionment 19 percent lights; December call unregistered; the synthetic verdict is scored
flags.detail: November Mainline apportionment is Light 19 percent and Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert (Enbridge notice, Oct 20), with Light 13 percent at Cromer and Heavy 16 percent at Superior. December's nowcast is naive persistence on those levels and no December judgment call is registered; nominations close Tuesday Nov 17 at 0700 MST. The synthetic return verdict is scored on the tape: Dec26 synthetic crude settled at +$5.70 on 300 lots on Oct 23, below both pre registered lines (+$7.00 and +$6.50); the Oct 26 file marked it +$5.75 on zero lots, which does not change the verdict. December WCS widened a second day on Oct 26, to -$29.25, but on only 50 lots, while the traded January export spread narrowed to +$7.80. Q3 volumes (Imperial and Cenovus Oct 30, Suncor Nov 3) are the fundamental check that can overrule the tape verdict. Trigger: A December judgment call registered, Q3 volumes contradicting the tape verdict, or a December apportionment notice

flags.title: Freight correction confirmed in Week 43; clean tankers at records; the TD3C benchmark is on trial in London
flags.detail: The Baltic Exchange Week 43 weekly (week ending Oct 23) is the latest Baltic print: TD3C WS 1208.13 with TCE $1,287,851 per day, TD22 at $58.22 million, TD9 at WS 666 with TCE under $210,400 per day, and clean routes at records (TC1 TCE $313,200, TC20 $336,400 per day). No Baltic daily assessment for Oct 26 was found in public sources, so a third week of correction is unconfirmed until Week 44. The Mercuria v Baltic Exchange trial opened Oct 26: Mercuria's opening filing aired panellist and internal doubts about TD3C assessments in March to April; the Baltic countered that panellists confirmed they could assess. No judgment has been reported and TD3C continues to publish; the case is an overhang on TD3C linked settlements, not an invalidation of any print. Trigger: A Week 44 Baltic print extending or reversing the correction, a trial judgment, or a fresh fixture at a materially different level

forward_calendar.what: Heating oil reserve bids due; private inventory survey
forward_calendar.detail: Bids close at 11:00 a.m. CT on the Oct 21 Northeast heating oil reserve exchange (up to 315,000 barrels), deliveries to complete by Nov 13. Bid uptake is a dated measure of how tight the Northeast distillate balance remains into winter, four days after the diesel crack closed below $100. The private survey for the week ending Oct 23 lands Tuesday afternoon, ahead of Wednesday's EIA report. No weekly bank forecast and no verifiable survey consensus for the week had published at this edition.

forward_calendar.what: EIA weekly report; Louisiana refiner third quarter call; Fed decision
forward_calendar.detail: The EIA reports the week ending Oct 23 at 10:30 a.m. ET. The refiner that received the Oct 23 emergency reserve exchange reports the same day (company schedule, Sep 16): the first on the record venue where the exchange's undisclosed cause can be asked. The Federal Reserve also decides on rates Wednesday.

forward_calendar.what: Imperial Oil and Cenovus Q3 results; positioning release
forward_calendar.detail: The first of the Canadian majors to report the quarter that contains the fall turnaround windows. Upstream volumes are the first public test of whether Syncrude, Horizon and the Suncor plants returned on their guided schedules; no completion notices have been published for any of them. The synthetic return verdict, scored on the tape at +$5.70, is graded against these volumes. The commitments of traders release the same day carries positioning as of Oct 27, the first vintage covering the episode's largest sessions.

forward_calendar.what: OPEC+ meeting (Nov 1 to 2, most likely Nov 2)
forward_calendar.detail: The seven core members set December levels. Their last decision (Oct 4) held November targets at September levels, a second straight monthly pause; no fresh delegate guidance dated Oct 26 or 27 was found. Actual output runs well below quota with Gulf exports war constrained, so the arithmetic is not the binding constraint on barrels.

forward_calendar.what: Suncor Q3 results; US midterm elections
forward_calendar.detail: Suncor operates Syncrude and the Base Plant and Edmonton refinery windows that ended in mid-October; its Q3 volumes are the closest public read on those returns ahead of September AER data. The midterms the same day are the date after which US strike expectations on Iran have been priced.
Vermilion reports the September quarter; volumes and any guidance change are the read.
MEG reports the September quarter; Christina Lake volumes are the read on the SAGD fleet's autumn.
Enbridge reports into the November apportionment month (Light 19 percent, Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert); Mainline volumes and any December colour are the read.
Deliveries under the Northeast heating oil reserve exchange (bids due Oct 27) complete by Nov 13, refilling the reserve ahead of the 2027 to 2028 heating season.

Nominations for December close at 0700 MST. December's nowcast is persistence at Light 19 percent and Heavy 7 percent; a judgment call registered before this date is the prediction programme's second decision performance entry.
